item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 100516
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Fri Oct 9 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Rachel, located several hundred miles west-northwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane
Simon, located about one hundred miles south of Manzanillo, Mexico.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form south of the coast of
Guatemala early next week. Environmental conditions are expected to
be conducive for gradual development thereafter, and a tropical
depression is likely to form by the middle or latter half of next
week as the system moves generally west-northwestward at around 10
mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 52
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 100247
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number  52
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026
 
...TROPICAL STORM WARNING ISSUED FOR THE EAST COAST OF BAJA
CALIFORNIA...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...23.8N 123.3W
ABOUT 720 MI...1160 KM SSW OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NE OR 50 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...995 MB...29.39 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has upgraded the Tropical Storm Watch to a
Tropical Storm Warning along the east coast of Baja California from
Isla San Luis northward to Puerto Penasco. The government of Mexico
has also issued a Tropical Storm Watch for the east coast of Baja
California from Bahia De Los Angeles northward to Isla San Luis, and
northwest Mexico from Puerto Libertad to Puerto Penasco.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California, from San Jose de Las Palomas
northward to the U.S./Mexico Border
* East coast of Baja California, from Isla San Luis northward to
Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Southern California coast from the U.S/Mexico Border northward to
the San Diego/Orange County Line
* East coast of Baja California, from Bahia De Los Angeles
northward to Isla San Luis
* Northwest Mexico from Puerto Libertad to Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests in northern Baja California, northern Gulf of California,
and Southern California should continue to monitor the progress of
Rachel.
 
For storm information specific to your area in the United
States, including possible inland watches and warnings, please
monitor products issued by your local National Weather Service
forecast office. For storm information specific to your area
outside of the United States, please monitor products issued by
your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was 
located near latitude 23.8 North, longitude 123.3 West. Rachel is 
moving toward the northeast near 9 mph (15 km/h). A general 
northeast to north-northeast motion, with a significant increase in 
forward speed, is expected over the next couple of days. On the 
forecast track, the center of Rachel is expected to approach the 
northern Baja California Peninsula or Southern California late 
Saturday or early Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Some strengthening is possible the next day or so, but rapid 
weakening forecast after the storm moves inland over the 
southwestern United States on Sunday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 995 mb (29.39 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected to reach portions of 
northern Baja California within the Tropical Storm Warning area 
starting Saturday evening into Sunday morning. Tropical storm 
conditions are also possible within the Tropical Storm Watch area in 
extreme Southern California, eastern Baja California and portions of 
northwest Mexico beginning late Saturday night or early Sunday. 
Strong gusty winds associated with the system are expected to spread 
over interior portions of the Southwest United States, especially in 
areas of higher terrain, from this weekend into early next week.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain to portions of
Baja California this weekend.
 
Rachel and associated moisture of the system will also bring
rainfall of 1 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5
inches in portions of the Southwest United States this weekend. This
will lead to increasing coverage of rainfall and potential for flash
and urban flooding.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and
the Flash Flood Risk graphic at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Swells partly generated by Rachel will build along the coast
of Southern California and northern Baja California through the
weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions, as well as moderate to isolated major
coastal flooding, through early next week.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1100 PM PDT.
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 52
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 100250
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  52
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026
 
Rachel has begun accelerating toward the northeast this evening. 
After a day or two of relatively unimpressive convection, shower and 
thunderstorm activity has increased near and east of the center, 
with cold cloud top temperatures below -65 C. However, dry mid-level 
air and moderate southwesterly wind shear continue to inhibit the 
development of organized deep convection around the center. Recent 
objective and subjective Dvorak intensity estimates range from 33-42 
kt. The intensity is maintained at 40 kt for this advisory.

The tropical storm is moving northeastward, or 50/08 kt. Rachel is 
positioned to the southeast of a strengthening closed mid-level low 
moving southeastward off the coast of California. A rapid 
acceleration toward the northeast then north-northeast is expected 
over the next 24-36 h as the low rounds the base of the trough. This 
motion should bring Rachel inland over northern Baja California late 
Saturday or early Sunday. Interaction with the low will subject 
Rachel to considerable wind shear, likely causing the low- and 
mid-level centers to decouple. The low-level center is likely to 
disintegrate as it encounters the Peninsular Ranges of northern 
Baja, while the mid-level center continues northeastward into the 
southwestern U.S. Track guidance remains similar to the previous 
cycle, with the hurricane regional models, the GFS, and the ECMWF on 
the left side of the envelope, and the GDMI and HCCA on the right. 
However, the spread is beginning to narrow, with guidance 
increasingly converging on landfall location in northern Baja. The 
latest NHC track forecast is very similar to the previous advisory, 
and lies near the middle of the guidance. 
 
A modest increase in intensity is expected over the next 24 h as 
Rachel interacts with the closed low, which will likely provide 
favorable upper-level dynamics and an increase in mid-level 
moisture. In addition, anomalously warm waters prevail offshore of 
Baja California. Rachel is forecast to strengthen into a strong 
tropical storm up through landfall, despite a significant increase 
in wind shear. After landfall, Rachel is expected to weaken rapidly 
as it moves inland and encounters the mountainous terrain, while the 
mid-level low continues into the southwestern U.S. Strong, gusty 
downslope winds may develop in the lee of the mountain ranges and 
extend into the deserts. However, Rachel is forecast to lose its 
tropical characteristics shortly after landfall. The latest NHC 
forecast intensity is near the middle of the guidance envelope. 

 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rachel is expected to approach the coast of the northern Baja
California Peninsula and extreme Southern California at tropical
storm strength Saturday night. Tropical storm conditions are
expected over portions of northern Baja California, Mexico where
Tropical Storm Warnings are in effect. Tropical storm conditions are
possible in extreme Southern California, eastern Baja California 
and portions of northwest Mexico where a Tropical Storm Watch is in 
effect.
 
2. Damaging wind gusts associated with Rachel and its remnants are
expected to spread over portions of northwestern Mexico and interior
portions of the Southwest United States, especially in areas of
higher terrain, Saturday night and Sunday.
 
3. Rachel and its moisture will spread over portions of the
Southwest United States and northern Baja California peninsula
through this weekend. This will lead to increasing coverage of
rainfall and for the potential for significant flash and urban
flooding.
 
4. Swells partly generated by Rachel will continue to build along
the coast of Southern California and northern Baja California.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions, as well as moderate to isolated major coastal
flooding, through early next week.  Please consult products from
your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  10/0300Z 23.8N 123.3W   40 KT  45 MPH
 12H  10/1200Z 25.3N 121.0W   45 KT  50 MPH
 24H  11/0000Z 28.9N 118.1W   50 KT  60 MPH
 36H  11/1200Z 33.9N 116.0W   40 KT  45 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 48H  12/0000Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 11a
item.description:
Issued at 1200 AM CST Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 100546
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Intermediate Advisory Number 11A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
1200 AM CST Sat Oct 10 2026
 
...SIMON BECOMES A CATEGORY 4 HURRICANE...
...PREPARATIONS TO PROTECT LIFE AND PROPERTY SHOULD BE RUSHED TO 
COMPLETION...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 AM CST...0600 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.0N 104.6W
ABOUT 140 MI...225 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 245 MI...395 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...140 MPH...220 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 1 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...945 MB...27.91 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Punta Mita to El Roblito
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued
36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Additional watches or warnings could be required for portions of the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 AM CST (0600 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 17.0 North, longitude 104.6 West. Simon is moving
toward the north near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this general motion with 
is forecast through the weekend.  On the forecast track, Simon is 
expected to be near or just inland of the west-central coast of 
Mexico later today or Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 140 mph (220 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Small Simon is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  Additional rapid strengthening is expected 
during the next day or so.  Simon is forecast to approach the of 
west-central Mexico as a major hurricane this evening or Sunday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80
miles (130 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 945 mb (27.91 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND:  Hurricane conditions are expected in the Hurricane Warning
area this evening or Sunday, with tropical storm conditions
expected later this morning.  Hurricane conditions are possible in 
the Hurricane Watch area beginning Sunday afternoon, with tropical 
storm conditions possible as soon as Sunday morning.  Tropical 
storm conditions are possible within the Tropical Storm Watch area 
beginning later this morning.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 10 to 20
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals of 30 inches possible across portions of Michoacan, Colima,
Jalisco and Nayarit through Sunday.  This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE:  A dangerous storm surge is likely along the
immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes
landfall. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and
destructive waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Roberts

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 100240
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
900 PM CST Fri Oct 09 2026
 
Small, compact Simon is rapidly intensifying this evening.  A
dreaded pinhole eye has formed and is now visible in the
infrared BD-curve enhancement.  Visible imagery shows that the tiny
eye is cloud-filled.  Based on the impressive satellite
presentation, the initial intensity is increased to 105 kt for this
advisory.  Simon's wind radii were adjusted based on an OSCAT-3
overpass.
 
Further rapid strengthening is expected over the next 24 hours, with
the forecast showing a peak intensity of 135 kt.  Because of
Simon's small inner core size, peak intensities are virtually
impossible to predict, and with just a slight warming of the
tiny eye, Simon could quickly become stronger than reflected in the
intensity forecast.  No changes worth noting were made to the NHC
intensity forecast, which continues to be above the guidance suite.
 
Simon's initial motion is estimated to be northward, or 360/6 kt.
The cyclone is moving within southerly mid-level steering flow
produced by high pressure over southern Mexico and a longwave
mid-tropospheric trough to the west stretching south-southwestward
from the southwest U.S.  It's still somewhat uncertain if Simon
will move inland over the Mexican states of Colima and Jalisco or
remain offshore.  The model fields of the skilled HiRes global
models (GFS/ECMWF/UKMET/CMC) show the cyclone moving inland
and rapidly weakening with dissipation over the rugged mountainous
terrain of the aforementioned states of Mexico in 60 hrs.  Of
course, if Simon's track remains just offshore, as a few of
the guidance indicates, it's likely that it will maintain hurricane
strength for a longer period of time.  As the previous
advisories indicated, the NHC forecast continues to favor the
former scenario (inland/weakening), sticking with the more skilled
consensus aids.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a
Hurricane warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita.
Preparations to protect life and property should be completed by
late today.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
3. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico through the weekend. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
